proof: For primitive odd real billiards in a fixed strict noncircular confocal pair, invert the original vertices about each original focus and join each list by straight segments. The two signed areas have a positive constant product on every admitted oriented family, including stars. Reversal preserves the product; r repeats multiply it by r².

The normalized flag double cover has four branch points and genus one. The four common isotropic tangents are the sole focal pole sources. Each of the four sigma-fixed flags has a different T-orbit when N is odd because 2j=0 mod N forces j=0. The two possible adjacent vertex poles at each flag are in one reciprocal coordinate so its determinant contains no fourth-order term. Reversal removes the second order term and the opposite area vanishes. Positivity from the focally oriented edge determinants shows the polar and zero divisors are exact.

Two explicit triangle phases produce 5/256 at a²=8,b²=5. Two valid even orbits with the same caustic give 1/10 and 169/1600. This differs from the other manuscript's single-focus area product. Earlier RGH apparent sign at one finite control and Ferudun's erroneous finite rectangle coordinates do not enter the native proof.
